cases.sentence: The editor said that the reviewer would revise the chapter after lunch.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Revise projects a V' taking the definite NP the chapter as its complement. Separately, after projects a PP containing the bare temporal NP lunch. The PP is not attached to the revision predicate in this analysis; it remains available for attachment to the subsequently constructed saying predicate. Determiners occupy Spec-NP. Traditional GB subject placement is adopted: finite subjects will be introduced in Spec-IP, without VP-internal subject positions or subject-raising chains.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded predicate and an unattached temporal PP.

relations.relation: Nominative Case assignment by finite I
Modal selection of a bare verbal predicate

derivationStages.stageRecord: The reviewer is base-generated in embedded Spec-IP, while would occupies finite I and selects the existing bare-form VP. The embedded subject receives the revision predicate's external theta-role and nominative Case from would. That projects the finite declarative CP, which said takes as its propositional complement. Only after this matrix V' has been built is the previously separate PP right-adjoined to it. The resulting higher V' contains said, its entire CP complement, and the temporal adjunct. Consequently after lunch locates the saying event, while the time of revising is not specified by this PP. This is direct attachment, not extraposition or movement out of the embedded clause.
derivationStages.statement: Build the reported clause and attach after lunch to the matrix predicate.

relations.relation: Nominative Case assignment by finite I
Finite tense licensing of the inflected lexical verb

values.realization: lexically inflected said; no overt head movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The editor is introduced in matrix Spec-IP and receives the saying predicate's external theta-role. Silent finite past I licenses nominative Case on the subject and the lexically inflected verb said. No overt affix lowering or lexical V-to-I movement is posited; would likewise remains in the embedded I position where it was introduced. A silent declarative C projects the root CP. The final interpretation places the editor's report after lunch, not necessarily the reviewer's revision. No movement or binding chain is needed, and the temporal PP remains outside the embedded CP.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix clause with the high temporal-attachment reading.

cases.sentence: Ik denk dat Noor het boek zal lezen.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines het with boek, forming a nominal object labeled by D. This object then merges with lezen, which selects it and assigns the internal thematic role. The lexical verb projects a head-final structure, appropriate to the Dutch embedded predicate. Labels identify the projecting lexical item or category rather than stipulated X-bar levels; the displayed child order records linearization, not an ordering intrinsic to Merge.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded lexical predicate and its definite object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Zal merges with the existing lexical predicate and projects Mod. This analysis treats zal as a modal auxiliary in an ascending auxiliary–infinitive cluster: the modal precedes its selected verbal domain, although lezen follows its nominal complement inside that domain. The modal introduces the prospective interpretation and requires an infinitival lexical predicate. This cluster order is a sentence-specific structural commitment, not a claim that all Dutch functional heads are head-initial.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the modal auxiliary above the lexical predicate.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge takes the object from its previously established complement position and remerges it at the edge of the modal projection. This local object displacement derives het boek zal lezen while retaining the lexical verb's thematic relation to the lower occurrence. The higher occurrence is pronounced; the complete lower copy is retained but silenced. The displacement remains below the subsequently introduced external argument and does not move the object into the embedded clause's subject position.
derivationStages.statement: Place the object to the left of the auxiliary by Internal Merge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent, head-final transitive v merges with the modal domain. Noor then merges at the edge of the resulting v projection as the external argument of the reading event. The proper name is treated as an atomic nominal D object. Transitive v licenses accusative on the object chain, whose displaced occurrence is already within its complement domain. The modal does not introduce an additional thematic subject.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce Noor as the embedded external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent, head-final T merges with the embedded v projection. It establishes present finiteness with the modal zal and agrees with Noor, licensing nominative and third-person singular agreement. The whole-word terminal zal supplies the finite modal form; this analysis does not split that word into separately realized morphemes. T's subject requirement triggers Internal Merge of Noor from its established external-argument position to the edge of T. Only the higher subject copy is pronounced. In this dat-clause the modal remains in the verbal domain rather than moving to C.
derivationStages.statement: Build embedded finite T and raise Noor to its subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The overt complementizer dat externally merges with the completed finite T projection and labels the resulting object C. Dat precedes its complement and marks the clause as a declarative complement. Its presence is consistent with the absence of embedded verb-second movement: the embedded subject remains at the edge of T, and zal remains in the lower verbal cluster.
derivationStages.statement: Close the embedded declarative clause with dat.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Denk selects the completed dat-clause as its propositional complement and projects a head-final lexical V structure. A silent, head-final matrix v then merges with that predicate, and Ik externally merges at its edge as the experiencer of the thinking state. The entire embedded clause remains intact inside the matrix verb's complement; its surface position after denk will result from matrix verb movement rather than from extraposition.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix predicate and introduce Ik.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix lexical V undergoes local head movement to the previously established v head. The resulting head is labeled v and contains the raised lexical verb together with the silent v item. The lexical source occurrence remains in its original position as a silent copy. This intermediate workspace makes the local V-to-v step explicit before the complex head moves into T.
derivationStages.statement: Move the matrix lexical verb into v.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Silent, head-final matrix T first merges with the existing v projection. The complex v head moves into T, preserving the preceding V-to-v step inside the raised head and silencing its lower copy. T agrees with the still-low Ik, licensing nominative and first-person singular agreement. Ik then internally merges at the edge of T, and its external-argument copy becomes silent. Denk is retained as a whole-word finite terminal; the abstract tense and agreement specifications do not require a separate morphological realization group. Both the T head and this intermediate subject position are now available for subsequent matrix verb-second movement.
derivationStages.statement: Establish matrix finiteness and the intermediate subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative C first merges to the left of the matrix T projection. Its verb-second requirement attracts the already formed T head into C, retaining silent copies at T, v, and V. Its edge requirement then attracts Ik from the previously established T-edge position into the single preverbal position at the edge of C. The intermediate subject occurrence is silenced along with the original external-argument occurrence. The resulting pronounced sequence is Ik denk dat Noor het boek zal lezen. The sentence has a matrix propositional-complement structure, an embedded subject Noor, and a locally displaced embedded object het boek; no additional structurally distinct reading is required by this input.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix verb-second clause.

cases.sentence: Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı mektubu Mehmet bugün okudu.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses head-final X-bar structures and the traditional GB placement of external arguments in Spec-IP. Ayşe’nin is the genitive subject of the nominalized relative clause, not a possessor of the external noun. Dün adjoins to the relative VP and modifies the writing event. Yazdığı takes a silent NP operator as its object; this position will become the relative-clause gap. In the separate matrix IP, Mehmet is the subject, mektubu is the object of okudu, and bugün adjoins to the matrix VP. The matrix clause therefore starts in subject–object–verb order; the sentence-initial object will be derived by scrambling. The lexical words are entered already inflected: yazdığı contains the nominalizing participial morphology and third-person singular agreement, while mektubu contains accusative morphology. Their internal morphemes are not represented as separate terminals. Abstract I heads represent the corresponding inflectional features. Both verbs assign Agent and Theme roles. Matrix I licenses nominative on Mehmet, and each verb governs and licenses accusative on its object; the relative operator's case is abstract and unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative-clause and matrix-clause base structures.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Yazdığı raises from the V position shown in the preceding workspace and adjoins to the relative I head. Its original position becomes an unpronounced verbal trace. This lexicalist GB analysis moves the already-inflected word rather than deriving its spelling by combining separately represented morphemes. The resulting I complex checks the participial and agreement features. Nominalized I licenses genitive on Ayşe’nin, and Spec-head agreement connects that subject to the third-person singular agreement of yazdığı. The operator remains in the object position: its subsequent A-bar movement has not yet occurred. The separate matrix IP is unchanged because relative-clause formation is still being completed.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb to nominalized I and license its genitive subject.

values.licensing: local government by the verbal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative C projects a head-final CP over the nominalized IP. The null operator moves from the previously established object position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace. The operator A-bar binds that trace, producing the open relative predicate ‘the entity that Ayşe wrote yesterday’. The Theme role and abstract object Case belong to the chain through its base position. The object trace remains locally governed by the verbal trace, which belongs to the V-to-I chain. Neither the operator nor C is pronounced. The matrix clause remains separate until this relative CP can be attached to its nominal head.
derivationStages.statement: Form the relative CP by moving the null object operator.

values.interpretation: restrictive modification of the letter as the Theme of Ayşe's writing

derivationStages.stageRecord: The completed CP adjoins on the left of the object's N′, giving the prenominal restrictive relative Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı. Its operator variable is identified with the external nominal head mektubu. The external noun is not moved out of the relative clause: this is a head-external operator analysis. Its accusative Case comes from the matrix verb, independently of the relative object's abstract Case. After attachment, okudu raises from its previously shown V position to matrix I and leaves a verbal trace. The resulting inflectional head agrees with Mehmet and retains past tense. The entire modified object is still in the matrix verb's complement position, so this workspace explicitly supplies the source for the later object scrambling.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the relative clause to the object noun and raise the matrix verb.

values.licensing: local government by the verbal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: The entire accusative NP moves from the matrix complement position established in the preceding stage to a left-adjoined position on IP. The relative clause travels with its nominal head; no extraction from the relative clause occurs. An unpronounced NP trace remains as the matrix verb's complement. This analysis treats the clause-peripheral scrambling as an A-bar dependency, with the lower position preserving the object's Theme role and accusative licensing. Mehmet remains in Spec-IP, and bugün remains a matrix VP adjunct. The resulting pronounced order is exactly Ayşe’nin dün yazdığı mektubu Mehmet bugün okudu. The sentence means that Mehmet read today the letter that Ayşe wrote yesterday. The two temporal adverbs modify their respective writing and reading events; the structure does not impose a separate contrastive or topical discourse interpretation on the fronted object.
derivationStages.statement: Scramble the complete object NP to the left edge and complete the sentence.

cases.sentence: A tanár a diákoknak adta a könyveket.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Each article externally merges with its noun, producing a D-labeled object without stipulated bar levels. The subject is singular and nominative, the recipient is plural and dative, and the theme is plural and accusative. The inflected nouns and adta are retained as whole-word terminals rather than decomposed into morphological pieces. Adta has past tense, third-person singular subject agreement, and definite-object conjugation. Unlike the multiple-topic analysis, this derivation will place a diákoknak in the immediately preverbal identificational-focus position, with A tanár outside it as a topic.
derivationStages.statement: Assemble the nominal expressions and select the finite verb for the recipient-focus reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb merges first with the theme a könyveket. The recipient then merges at the edge of the resulting V-labeled object. This binary VP shell gives the dative an argument position from which it can subsequently move to focus. It is not generated directly in the left periphery, and it is not a displaced possessor of könyveket, which lacks possessive morphology.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the verb's theme and recipient domain.

derivationStages.stageRecord: An unpronounced transitive v merges with the lexical predicate, and the subject merges at the edge of the v-labeled object. The teacher receives the agent role there. Transitive v licenses accusative on the theme, while the recipient's dative remains lexically licensed. Neither the subject nor the recipient has yet entered the discourse field.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the teacher as the external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The lexical verb moves from the V position established earlier to v, producing a complex v head. The lower lexical copy becomes unpronounced, and the higher occurrence currently realizes adta. This intermediate position is retained explicitly because the next movement step takes the complex v head, not the original unmoved V, to T.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the lexical verb to the light-verb head.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Past T merges above the v domain, agrees with the third-person singular subject, and licenses its nominative case. The definite direct object licenses the verb's definite conjugation. The complex v head then moves to T, leaving an unpronounced lower occurrence. The lexical terminal in the higher complex head realizes the whole word adta; no separate surface realization is assigned to abstract v or T. No obligatory subject movement to a specifier of T is assumed, so both nominal arguments remain available for their distinct discourse-driven movements.
derivationStages.statement: Build the finite tense domain and establish agreement.

values.effect: focused recipient immediately precedes the finite verb

derivationStages.stageRecord: Foc merges above the tense domain and attracts the recipient from its established lower argument position to its specifier. The activated focus head then attracts the complex T head from its preceding-stage position, placing the pronounced verb immediately after the focused dative. A higher topic head attracts the subject from the v edge, and silent declarative C completes the clause. All lower moved occurrences are unpronounced. With focal stress on diákoknak, the reading is approximately 'It was to the students that the teacher gave the books,' identifying the students against contextual alternative recipients. The preverbal dative separates the subject from the verb, so this is not a subject-identificational-focus structure. The topic reading and this focus reading are both supported because the written input supplies no disambiguating stress contour.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the recipient-focus declarative structure.
